short: The military coup that expelled moderate members of Parliament, leaving a radical "Rump" to try King Charles I.
full:
On 6 December 1648, soldiers of the New Model Army under the command of Colonel Thomas Pride forcibly prevented conservative and moderate Members of Parliament from entering the House of Commons. The army had become frustrated with Parliament's continued negotiations with King Charles I despite his role in provoking the Second English Civil War. Around 230 members were purged, and another 45 were temporarily arrested.

The event constituted the only military coup d'état in English history. The remaining 80 or so members, known as the Rump Parliament, were largely compliant with the army's radical agenda. This cleared the constitutional path for the unprecedented trial and execution of the king the following month, dismantling the monarchy and establishing the English Republic.
